exposure: difficulties with embryo transfer due to distorted anatomy

Women with a large niche (residual myometrium <3 mm) and complaints of either postmenstrual spotting, dysmenorrhea, intrauterine fluid accumulation, and/or difficulties with embryo transfer due to distorted anatomy
outcome: Reduction of the main problem (postmenstrual spotting, dysmenorrhea, intrauterine fluid accumulation, and/or difficulties with embryo transfer)
cohort: 101 women with a large niche (residual myometrium <3 mm) and complaints of either postmenstrual spotting, dysmenorrhea, intrauterine fluid accumulation and/or difficulties with embryo transfer due to distorted anatomy
finding: Laparoscopic niche resection was found to be effective in reducing postmenstrual spotting, dysmenorrhea, and intrauterine fluid, as well as increasing residual myometrium thickness in women with a large niche.
